---
title: "all() of an empty vector is TRUE"
ref: LEN-01
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'all(logical(0))'
reponse: 'TRUE'
attendu: "`FALSE`, since the vector holds no `TRUE`"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2023), safer-r"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
all(logical(0))

grades <- c(12, 15, 9)
all(grades[grades > 20] >= 10)
```
:::

## Why

It is the mathematical convention: a property holds for every element of an empty set, since no element contradicts it. `any()` follows the opposite convention and returns `FALSE`.

The danger comes from the filter upstream. When `grades[grades > 20]` keeps nothing, the `all(...)` test passes, and the `if` that depends on it runs as if everything were fine. Same thing with `all(c(NA, NA), na.rm = TRUE)`, which is `TRUE`.

## The fix

Check the length before drawing a conclusion.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
selection <- grades[grades > 20]
length(selection) > 0 && all(selection >= 10)
```
:::
